summary: Oscillating 5xx surge from adaptive throttle misprediction and runtime memory reclamation during mixed-embedding/chat traffic
description:
Issue summary:
We observed an elevated and oscillating 5xx rate impacting a single enterprise tenant (AuroraMaps) in us-east. Error patterns correlate with API Gateway throttling spikes and upstream runtime processes being forcibly reclaimed / OOM-killed. The symptom set looks like a misprediction in the adaptive throttler combined with memory pressure in a subset of runtime pods serving mixed embedding and chat workloads.

Impact:
- ~15% of AuroraMaps requests in the window returned 502/503/504 intermittently (streaming and non-streaming routes).
- Latency for successful requests increased (p50 -> +120ms, p95 -> +800ms).
- Customer reported degraded user experience for map annotation features using chat + embedding mix; ticket raised via support channel.

Environment:
- prod-us-east cluster (k8s), mixed node types (A100 and T4 pools).
- Affected model variants: rwd-13b-quant-v2 (embedding-heavy), rwd-chat-7b-compat (chat sessions).
- Traffic pattern: sudden concurrent embedding bulk uploads + many long-lived chat streams from same tenant.

Timeline (local times):
- 2026-03-13T14:18Z: First alert from Grafana (error-rate spike on apigw-us-east).
- 2026-03-13T14:20Z: Support alerted SRE and customer; initial triage started.
- 2026-03-13T14:25Z: Observed runtime pod restarts; kernel messages show memory_reclaim invoked and killer invoked on cgroup tasks.
- 2026-03-13T14:40Z: Temporary mitigation applied (see Mitigation).

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) From a single tenant in prod-us-east, start a mix: concurrent embedding bulk upload (small-batch parallelized) + ~200 concurrent long-lived streaming chat sessions.
2) Observe accept-queue growth at apigw and throttler marking more aggressive shedding policy.
3) After throttle engages, backpressure causes hedged retries and request fanout that drives certain runtime pods into heavy memory churn and kernel reclamation.

Observed logs / metrics / traces:
- Grafana panel: apigw error-rate spiked to 18% at peak; upstream 502/503 logs show short-lived connection resets and 504 timeouts. (link: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/alerts/apigw-us-east?from=...)
- Kernel logs on impacted runtimes: "kswapd0 high memory reclaim" and repeated "oom-killer: Kill process 14231 (runtime_worker) score 912" entries.
- Runtime logs: repeated GC-like pause messages, KV-cache eviction thrash, and the serving runtime logged "memory pressure: reclaim fallback" before exit.
- Traces show high queueing delay at apigw (acceptqueue length) and hedged retry amplification for streaming routes.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Support/SRE advised customer to throttle embedding bulk upload parallelism for AuroraMaps. Customer applied application-side rate-limit (reduced concurrency by 60%).
- We muted hedged retries at apigw for the tenant route to avoid retry amplification (config change rolled to canary then to entire us-east apigw pool at 14:38Z).
- Increased autoscaler warm headroom for the A100 runtime pool serving the tenant by +2 replicas to provide extra memory capacity during warmup.
- Marked two runtime nodes as drained and rotated them after kernel-level memory reclaim evidence.

Investigation notes / hypothesis:
- Hypothesis A: Adaptive throttler mispredicted working set because it used short-window token-rate features; sudden mix of embedding + streaming caused acceptance heuristic to swing too low, causing apigw to enforce harsh shedding. That shed traffic into retry loops which amplified demand on the runtime pool.
- Hypothesis B: Long-lived chat sessions pinned KV-cache slots while embedding bulk created burst memory allocations (for batched tokenization / embedding tensors). Combination caused host OOM reclaim of cgroup slices and killed some runtime workers.
- Evidence: correlated kernel OOM lines with times of bursty embedding operations; heap profiles from one runtime show transient large allocations around embedding batching code paths.
- Alternate contributing factor: hedged-retry policy at the gateway caused duplicate work to be sent to runtimes when latency spiked, magnifying memory footprint.

Immediate next steps (owner: Ravi Patel):
- Collect full heap profiles from a surviving runtime pod and upload to S3 for heapdiff analysis (tasked, ETA 2026-03-14 11:00Z).
- Reproduce in staging with synthetic mixed workload (owner: SRE QA) and validate throttler prediction smoothing changes.
- Instrument toggles to disable hedged retries per-tenant as a short-term safety valve (dev ticket created).
- Add a quota guard on embedding batch concurrency per-tenant in apigw (product follow-up).

Longer-term actions:
- Adjust adaptive throttler to include longer-window memory-pressure signals and a smoothing window for sudden bimodal payloads.
- Add per-tenant memory-accounting in scheduler to avoid overcommitting runtime node memory when multiple heavy-tenants run mixed workloads.
- Postmortem runbook and customer communication template (owner: CS/Support).

Customer communication status:
- AuroraMaps notified via support email at 14:30Z; they confirmed reduced throughput is acceptable as temporary workaround. They requested a root-cause summary and ETA for permanent fix.
